findings.text: non-blocking: the delivered-record test reads only the parent directory's name, where reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:174 also anchors on the runs root, so a declared path under any directory named review-records/ is judged delivered here that the filer would ignore, and a review can be refused for a record no promotion would read; the code is moved from the inline base body, so this change carries the gap rather than introducing it.

non-blocking: _refused_delivered_review_read already walks declared review-record paths, parses each and asks review.store_review_refusals, while reckon/crew_run_commands.py:3315 repeats that traversal and aggregation instead of calling or extending it, so what counts as a delivered record must change in both places.

non-blocking: the accepted-paths widening has no test -- both green cases write the record on a path the run already declared, so dropping the accepted list from the declaration at :3315 leaves every assertion in tests/test_review_record_contract.py true while the widen path silently stops being checked.

non-blocking: **_kwargs accepts any keyword the rule passes, so the double no longer pins the one-argument call shape the lambda it replaces did; naming the keyword would keep that check while still allowing the snapshot the rule now passes.
